corticotropin-re- lasing factor (CRF)-induced long-lasting potentiation, like tetanization-induced late phase long-term potentiation, requires protein synthesis, that CRF neurons may be involved in long-term potentiation in the hippocampus, and that CRF-induced long- lasting potentiation and tetanus-induced long-term potentia- tion share common mechanisms.

CRF produces a long-lasting potentiated response in the rat hippocampus that depends on protein synthesis and that the CRF mRNA level was increased after LTP recording, suggesting a possible role for CRF in LTP.
CRF induces a protein synthesis-dependent long-lasting potentiation that requires the participation of CRF neurons.

the mechanism of long-lasting potentiation induced by CRF in rat hippocampal neurons.
the role of corticotropin-relinse factor (CRF), a hypothalamic neuropeptide, in the regulation of hippocampal function.
the mechanism of CRF-induced long-term potentiations in the hippocampus.
